elements.quote: The urgent need for immediate solutions to tackle public health emergencies of international concern undermines effective coordination and collaboration between researchers 1,2 . Since the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) outbreak was reported in December 2019, a huge number of clinical studies have been initiated, firstly in China, South Korea, then subsequently in Europe, Japan, North America and Australia. The number of trials recorded in clinical trial registries is proliferating exponentially, with many independent research efforts designed to answer similar questions. Whilst multicentred trials can potentially improve generalisability of study results across widely divergent endemic settings, this requires comparable study designs and comparators. Conversely, independent trials with small sample sizes and underrepresentation of some patient populations limit the acquisition of substantive evidence to assess the effects and applicability of the many diagnostic methods, therapeutic and prophylactic strategies targeted to address the COVID-19 pandemic 3 .
elements.reason: The introduction explicitly describes the current state of knowledge (rapid proliferation of trial registrations, geographic spread) and key uncertainties/limitations (many small, independent trials, underrepresentation of populations, heterogeneity), satisfying the requirement to describe current knowledge and uncertainties.

elements.quote: Background: Since the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) outbreak was first reported in December 2019, many independent trials have been planned that aim to answer similar questions. Tools allowing researchers to review studies already underway can facilitate collaboration, cooperation and harmonisation. The Infectious Diseases Data Observatory (IDDO) has undertaken a living systematic review (LSR) to provide an open, accessible and frequently updated resource summarising characteristics of COVID-19 study registrations.
elements.reason: The abstract and manuscript state the importance of providing an open, frequently updated resource to summarise study registrations and explain how such a review facilitates collaboration, harmonisation and avoidance of duplication, which explains the need for conducting the review.

No explicit statement was found in the provided evidence explaining the need for the current review in the context of existing similar systematic reviews, nor citation/discussion of prior reviews or justification as an update/replication.

This conditional item applies to reviews of intervention effects. The provided evidence describes a living review of clinical trial registrations and does not present assessment of intervention effects or propose mechanisms of action; thus the requirement does not apply to this manuscript based on the available text.

The conditional item concerns inclusion of a logic model for complex interventions or delivery contexts. The supplied evidence does not present or propose a logic model and the review focuses on trial registrations rather than complex intervention delivery frameworks; therefore this requirement is not applicable based on the available text.

elements.quote: This is a living systematic review of clinical study registrations (clinical trials and otherwise) for the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of COVID-19, an important endeavour in the midst of the pandemic and a concurrent infodemic with rapid evidence proliferation.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the review's scope (clinical study registrations addressing diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of COVID-19), which describes the objective. However, it does not present the objectives or questions in a formal question‑formulation framework (e.g., PICO or similar), so the requirement for explicit objectives using a relevant framework is only partially met.

Although the review covers interventions (treatment and prevention are included in scope), there is no explicit statement of planned comparisons framed using PICO or an appropriate variant in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: All clinical trial registrations either being planned, or currently underway to diagnose, treat or prevent COVID-19 were eligible for inclusion in the baseline results of this review. This included patients known to be infected with COVID-19 as well as healthy volunteers, healthcare workers or other patient populations where health related outcomes were assessed in the context of COVID-19. The review was not limited by outcome, language or intervention given the desire to capture all clinical trial registrations planning to or currently evaluating any COVID-19 diagnostic, prevention or treatment modality. Eligibility was not restricted to clinical trials only; no limitations on study design were applied so that all research and observational studies would be incorporated, including retrospective studies.
elements.reason: The eligibility paragraph explicitly lists the types of records eligible (clinical trial registrations planned or underway), populations (infected patients, healthy volunteers, healthcare workers, other patient populations), and states no limitations on outcomes or study design—thus specifying study characteristics used to determine eligibility.

elements.quote: The review was not limited by outcome, language or intervention given the desire to capture all clinical trial registrations planning to or currently evaluating any COVID-19 diagnostic, prevention or treatment modality.
